script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Calling this the whole request overlooks David's request to preserve his life from dread of the enemy in verse 1.
The sword is a comparison, but the psalm does not say that nobody picks up a blade.
The psalm says they shoot suddenly, not that they hit their target.
The joke about a polite ambush makes light of the attack on the innocent.
The psalm does not answer who will see the hidden snares. Those who see in verse 8 are not said to see the snares.
The psalm does not say being spotted is their big worry. It says they shoot without fear.
The psalm does not state how sure they are that nobody will see the snares. That inference needs to be marked as Papa Dorin's own.
The psalm records their claim but does not say they are proud of it.
David uses the arrow comparison for the mob's bitter words; the psalm does not say the mob used that picture.
The knife joke makes the wicked and their injury the target of the humor.
The verse says their tongues are turned against them, not that their tongues are stopped.
The psalm says mankind will ponder what God has done, but it does not say how long anyone will remember it.
The psalm says the wicked will be wounded and made to stumble, but it does not say they are stopped.
